24% (n= 47) reported to have used apps, social media or websites for
their health. Social media was the preferred category to use for health
information, among both urban (25%) and rural (11%) participants,
with Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, and Twitter being the
most frequently mentioned platforms. Reasons included, to gain
knowledge, watch videos, chat with friends and look at posts. To
search for health information, social media was more commonly used
by rural students (12%) compared to urban students (8%). Conversely,
search engines were more popular among urban students (12%) than
rural students (5%). For discussing health topics online, social media
was the predominant platform in both urban (9%) and rural (8%)
areas.
